A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BlockScan study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A–D and checklist support reliable comparison despite reordering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v4 Section 5 and the appendices report original Ethereum and Solana detection experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations and supplementary evaluations.

after.justification: v5 Section 6 and the appendices retain these original empirical results, including detection performance, robustness tests and training-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The multimodal tokenizer, RoBERTa-based masked training with RoPE and FlashAttention, top-s prediction scoring and top-k detection remain unchanged. v4 Section 3, v5 Section 4 and Algorithm 1 describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Ethereum and Solana coverage, including the supplementary Ethereum evaluation with 100 attack transactions from 69 vulnerable contracts. The new background mentions other application areas without adding evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain BlockGPT, Doc2Vec, GPT-4o and Heuristic. The appendix post-detection and fine-tuning comparisons also retain their comparators. BERT4ETH is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported chronological 80/20 splits, top-k thresholds, FPR/recall/precision metrics, model configurations and training settings are unchanged. The appendix experiments retain their evaluation procedures and settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, mask/candidate/model-size sensitivity tests, noise experiment and FlashAttention/base-model studies are retained unchanged in Table 3 and Tables 8–10. Appendix C also retains the transaction-duplication analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three independent runs and repeat this information in the checklist. v5 introduces no additional seed information, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and findings in Tables 1–3, Tables 6–10 and Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, both report Solana BlockScan performance at k=20 as 72.22% recall, 65% precision and 0.47% FPR.

T1.justification: The domain-adaptation bound moves from Theorem 4.1 to Theorem 5.1 with unchanged definitions and reasoning. Algorithm 1 and Appendix D.2 retain the same loss, feature-extraction, contrastive-learning and KDE formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same methodological, performance, theoretical-guarantee and open-source novelty claims. The new contextual material does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline failures, component effects and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning evolving transaction patterns, attacks resembling benign behavior and GPT-4o fine-tuning constraints, alongside the same appendix discussion.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same pseudocode, dataset statistics, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, GPT-4o prompt and fine-tuning budget. Code, model and dataset access statements and the repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds five references supporting the new Background section and cites BERT4ETH in Related Work. It distinguishes BERT4ETH's account-level fraud detection from BlockScan's intra-transaction focus. Existing references and the broader related-work taxonomy are retained.

P1.justification: v5 inserts a short Background section, adds a BERT4ETH sentence and places the checklist before Appendices A–D. Section references and an author-footnote phrase are updated; the remaining narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The figures, tables and algorithm retain their designs and content, with changes in placement and surrounding layout. Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 4, while Figure 2 moves from page 17 to a dedicated page 26.

improvement.justification: The new Background section helps orient readers unfamiliar with blockchain and smart contracts, while the BERT4ETH discussion makes the research positioning more complete. These provide modest accessibility and contextual gains. Pagination becomes less compact, but the scientific evidence and reproducibility information are preserved.
